Read 10x Genomics Raw (Unfiltered) Feature Barcode Matrices

Source: R/rawMatrixFrom10x.R
rawMatrixFrom10x.Rd

The raw-matrix counterpart of seuratFrom10x(). Reads the unfiltered feature barcode matrix H5 – every barcode Cell Ranger saw, not just the ones it called as cells – for one or more runs, taking the same manifest / path / multi arguments.

Usage

rawMatrixFrom10x(
  manifest = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  multi = NULL,
  multiplexed = NULL
)

Arguments

manifest

Data frame with columns Path (character; path to each run's outs/ directory) and multi (logical). Rows may mix the two pipelines freely. Mutually exclusive with path.

path

Character string. Path to a single Cell Ranger outs/ directory. Mutually exclusive with manifest.

multi

Logical. Whether path was produced by cellranger multi rather than cellranger count – see the section above. Required when path is supplied; ignored when manifest is supplied, since the pipeline is read per-row from manifest$multi instead.

multiplexed

Deprecated. The former name of multi; still accepted, with a warning.

Value

A named list of sparse count matrices (features x barcodes), one per run, named after the directory above each outs/. Runs whose raw H5 is missing are dropped from the manifest-mode result with a warning; in path mode a missing file raises an error instead.

Details

This is the input a barcode rank plot needs. Cell calling is exactly the step that separates the raw matrix from the filtered one, so a plot meant to show where that cutoff landed cannot be drawn from the filtered matrix: the empty droplets that form the left-hand cliff have already been removed. Use plotBarcodeRanks() if drawing that plot is all you want; it calls this reader one run at a time and never holds more than one raw matrix in memory.

What is returned, and why it is not Seurat objects

Sparse count matrices, not Seurat objects. A raw matrix has one column per barcode in the GEM well – of order 10^5 to 10^6, the overwhelming majority of them empty droplets – and building a Seurat object means computing and storing per-cell metadata for all of them. Nothing downstream of a raw matrix wants that; barcode ranking needs only the column sums. Filtered matrices, which are already cell-called, are what seuratFrom10x() wraps in Seurat objects.

cellranger multi runs yield one matrix per run, not per sample

This is the one place where the return shape differs from seuratFrom10x(). cellranger multi writes a single run-level raw matrix at outs/multi/count/raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5, shared by every demuxed sample in the pool – cell calling happens once for the whole GEM well, and only afterwards are the called barcodes assigned to samples. There is therefore no per-sample raw matrix to read, and a multi = TRUE row expands to one entry named after the run directory rather than to N entries named after the demuxed samples.

Read that way, a barcode rank curve from a pooled run describes the pool, which is the level at which the knee is a meaningful diagnostic.

See also

plotBarcodeRanks(), which consumes these matrices one at a time; seuratFrom10x() for the filtered, cell-called matrices.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# One run
raw <- rawMatrixFrom10x(path = "/path/to/Sample_1/outs", multi = FALSE)
dim(raw[["Sample_1"]])

# A pool -- one matrix for the whole run, not one per demuxed sample
raw <- rawMatrixFrom10x(path = "/path/to/Pool1/outs", multi = TRUE)
names(raw)

# Several runs from a manifest. Watch memory: these are large.
manifest <- data.frame(
  Path  = c("/path/to/Sample_1/outs", "/path/to/Pool1/outs"),
  multi = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
raw <- rawMatrixFrom10x(manifest = manifest)

# Column sums are the barcode totals a rank plot is built from
totals <- Matrix::colSums(raw[[1]])
} # }
